711	
712	def _days_to_send(
713	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition], day_zero: date, days: int
714	) -> NDArray[numpy.int64]:
715	    """Choose which days of the window a claim's series carries to the reader.
716	
717	    **A cap on what is sent, never on what is worked out**, and a cap on the evenly
718	    spaced points alone. Ordinarily every day of the window. Past 180 days that is
719	    more points than anybody scrubs through, so a series is drawn at 180 evenly
720	    spaced days instead — **and every claim's own resolve-by day is kept whatever
721	    the cap says**, so a map judged on more than 180 different days sends one point
722	    per judged day, which is more than the cap and is the honest answer. That is not a nicety: a
723	    tile's headline number is read on the claim's own resolve-by day, and if that
724	    day were not on the claim's own series the number on the tile would not be a
725	    point of the line drawn beneath it.
726	
727	    It was once the grid the whole engine worked on, and that was a defect. A push
728	    fires on the day its cause is settled, read off the days worked out — so
729	    thinning them made that day depend on how long the window was, and an edit at
730	    one end of a map could re-time a claim at the other end that nothing connected
731	    it to. Measured before it was separated: an inserted claim that stretched a
732	    window from 31 days to 365 moved a claim in a wholly separate piece of the map
733	    by `.096`.
734	
735	    Args:
736	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
737	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
738	        days: How long the window is.
739	
740	    Returns:
741	        The days to send, in order.
742	    """
743	    judged = numpy.array(
744	        sorted({_day_index(one.resolution.by, day_zero, days) for one in claims.values()}),
745	        dtype=numpy.int64,
746	    )
747	    if days + 1 <= SERIES_CAP:
748	        return numpy.arange(days + 1, dtype=numpy.int64)
749	    spare = max(2, SERIES_CAP - len(judged))
750	    evenly = numpy.rint(numpy.linspace(0, days, spare)).astype(numpy.int64)
751	    return numpy.union1d(judged, evenly).astype(numpy.int64)
752	
753	
754	def _settled_days(
755	    order: Sequence[PropositionId],
756	    arrows_into: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[Link]],
757	    fixed_on: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[Assignment]],
758	    day_zero: date,
759	) -> dict[PropositionId, int]:
760	    """Say which day each claim's clock starts on — the day it is *settled*.
761	
762	    Three rules, in order. If an edit fixed the claim's value, its clock starts on
763	    the earliest day any of them holds from. Otherwise it starts on the earliest
764	    day a live incoming arrow reaches it: the day that arrow's cause was settled,
765	    plus the arrow's delay, rounded up to a whole day. A claim with neither is
766	    settled on day zero, because the map carries no timing information about it at
767	    all.
768	
769	    **Being settled is not being true.** A claim with nothing fixing it is sampled
770	    from its own prior in every draw; its clock starting says only when the arrows
771	    leaving it begin to measure their delays from. Conflating the two is the
772	    mistake this paragraph exists to prevent.
773	
774	    Args:
775	        order: Every claim, causes first.
776	        arrows_into: The ordinary arrows pointing at each claim.
777	        fixed_on: Every value fixed on each claim, in the order the edits were made.
778	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
779	
780	    Returns:
781	        The day each claim's clock starts on.
782	    """
783	    settled: dict[PropositionId, int] = {}
784	    for claim_id in order:
785	        fixed = fixed_on[claim_id]
786	        if fixed:
787	            settled[claim_id] = min(_day_index(one.at, day_zero) for one in fixed)
788	            continue
789	        arrivals = [math.ceil(settled[one.source] + one.lag) for one in arrows_into[claim_id]]
790	        settled[claim_id] = min(arrivals) if arrivals else 0
791	    return settled
792	
793	
794	def _shape_row(link: Link, settled: int, points: NDArray[numpy.int64]) -> Numbers:
795	    """Work out how big one arrow's push is on each day, as a fraction of its full size.
796	
797	    A plain function of elapsed days, and zero before the cause was settled. A
798	    **spike** is nothing through the delay, then full size, halving every half-life
799	    afterwards. A **step** is nothing through the delay, then full size, held. A
800	    **ramp** climbs from nothing to full size across the delay, then holds.
801	
802	    A ramp with no delay at all needs no special case: the days at or past the
803	    delay are settled first, which for a delay of nothing is every day from the
804	    cause onwards, and the climb is then left with no days to climb over. Such a
805	    ramp behaves as a step, as a consequence of the shape rather than as a rule.
806	
807	    A spike always says how fast it fades — a spike that does not is a fault in the
808	    map, refused by its own rules before it ever reaches here. The line below is
809	    the net under a map that arrived some other way, and it holds the push rather
810	    than dividing by nothing.
811	
812	    Args:
813	        link: The arrow.
814	        settled: The day the arrow's cause was settled.
815	        points: The days to work out.
816	
817	    Returns:
818	        One number per day, between 0 and 1.
819	    """
820	    elapsed = points.astype(numpy.float64) - settled
821	    landed = elapsed >= link.lag
822	    row = numpy.zeros_like(elapsed)
823	    row[landed] = 1.0
824	    if link.shape == "step":
825	        return row
826	    if link.shape == "ramp":
827	        climbing = (elapsed >= 0.0) & ~landed
828	        row[climbing] = elapsed[climbing] / link.lag
829	        return row
830	    if link.half_life is None or link.half_life <= 0.0:
831	        return row
832	    row[landed] = 2.0 ** (-(elapsed[landed] - link.lag) / link.half_life)
833	    return row
834	
835	
836	def _opposing(arrows: Sequence[Link], supposed: bool) -> list[Link]:
837	    """List the arrows pushing against a supposed value, in the order they were given.
838	
839	    An arrow opposes a claim supposed **true** when its push is negative, and one
840	    supposed **false** when its push is positive. An arrow of no strength pushes
841	    neither way and opposes nothing.
842	    """
843	    return [one for one in arrows if (one.strength < 0.0) == supposed and one.strength != 0.0]
844	
845	
846	def _spells_on(
847	    fixed: Sequence[Assignment],
848	    arrows: Sequence[Link],
849	    settled: Mapping[PropositionId, int],
850	    day_zero: date,
851	) -> tuple[_Spell, ...]:
852	    """Work out which stretch of days each edit's word holds over, on one claim.
853	
854	    Each edit's word holds from its own day until the next edit on the same claim
855	    has something to say, because a later assignment overrides an earlier one. A
856	    supposition also stops early, on the day the **cause** of the first arrow
857	    pushing against it was settled — not the day that arrow's push reaches full
858	    size, because tying the end of a supposition to the arrival would tie "do I
859	    still take your word for this" to a delay parameter.
860	
861	    A user may suppose a claim again after it was undermined. The second
862	    supposition holds from its own day until something undermines it again, and the
863	    series then reads supposed, withdrawn, pushed, supposed — which falls straight
864	    out of "a later assignment overrides an earlier one" rather than needing a rule
865	    of its own.
866	
867	    When two arrows undermine a supposition on the very same day, the one that
868	    arrived on the map first wins. That is the arrow's own place on the map, which
869	    is the order the edits added them in: the base map's arrows, then each `insert`'s
870	    arrows in the order it listed them. Some settled answer is needed or the badge
871	    would name a different arrow on different runs and a world would stop replaying.
872	
873	    Args:
874	        fixed: Every value fixed on this claim, in the order the edits were made.
875	        arrows: The ordinary arrows pointing at it, in the order the map carries them.
876	        settled: The day each claim's clock starts on.
877	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
878	
879	    Returns:
880	        One stretch per edit, in the order the edits were made.
881	    """
882	    where = {one.id: index for index, one in enumerate(arrows)}
883	    days = [_day_index(one.at, day_zero) for one in fixed]
884	    spells: list[_Spell] = []
885	    for index, one in enumerate(fixed):
886	        starts = days[index]
887	        ends = days[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(days) else None
888	        undermined_on, undermined_by = None, None
889	        if one.kind == "do":
890	            against = [
891	                (max(starts, settled[arrow.source]), where[arrow.id], arrow)
892	                for arrow in _opposing(arrows, one.value)
893	            ]
894	            live = [entry for entry in against if ends is None or entry[0] < ends]
895	            if live:
896	                undermined_on, _, undermined_by = min(live, key=lambda entry: entry[:2])
897	        spells.append(
898	            _Spell(
899	                kind=one.kind,
900	                value=one.value,
901	                starts=starts,
902	                ends=ends,
903	                undermined_on=undermined_on,
904	                undermined_by=undermined_by,
905	            )
906	        )
907	    return tuple(spells)
908	
909	
910	def _retractions(setup: _Setup, introduced_by: Mapping[LinkId, int]) -> tuple[Retraction, ...]:
911	    """Write down every supposition something undermined, and which edit is to blame.
912	
913	    **Which edit added the undermining arrow is always known**, and that is a
914	    theorem rather than a convention: supposing a claim cuts every arrow pointing
915	    at it at that moment, so any arrow that later pushes against it was added
916	    afterwards, by an edit with a position in the branch.
917	
918	    Args:
919	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
920	        introduced_by: Which edit added each arrow, by position in the branch.
921	
922	    Returns:
923	        One retraction per supposition that ended, claim by claim.
924	
925	    Raises:
926	        ValueError: If an arrow that undermined a supposition is not in the list of
927	            which edit added what. That is the one thing this file raises for, and
928	            it is a broken promise between our own two pieces of code rather than
929	            anything a user did: whoever asked for this world folded a branch onto
930	            the map and then did not say which edit added which arrow.
931	    """
932	    found: list[Retraction] = []
933	    for claim_id in sorted(setup.spells):
934	        for spell in setup.spells[claim_id]:
935	            if spell.undermined_on is None or spell.undermined_by is None:
936	                continue
937	            arrow = spell.undermined_by
938	            if arrow.id not in introduced_by:
939	                raise ValueError(
940	                    "A supposition was undermined by an arrow that nothing says was added "
941	                    "by an edit. Every arrow that can undermine a supposition was added "
942	                    "after it, so the branch's edits have to be passed in alongside the "
943	                    "values they fixed."
944	                )
945	            found.append(
946	                Retraction(
947	                    target=claim_id,

957	def _states(
958	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition],
959	    spells: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[_Spell]],
960	    shape_rows: Mapping[LinkId, Numbers],
961	    points: NDArray[numpy.int64],
962	) -> dict[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]]:
963	    """Name what each claim's every day is, so the canvas knows when a number would mislead.
964	
965	    On a claim no supposition ever touched, and on any day before one takes effect,
966	    the day is `sampled`. While a supposition holds it is `supposed`, and the tile
967	    shows the word rather than a likelihood. Once something has undermined it the
968	    day is `withdrawn` until an opposing push is actually live, and `pushed` after
969	    that. The gap between the two — the day the world changed and the day the push
970	    arrives — is the honest shape of the answer, not a bug to hide, which is the
971	    whole reason these words exist.
972	
973	    A claim reported to have happened is `sampled` throughout: an observation is
974	    news rather than a lever, so there is no word standing in for a number.
975	
976	    Args:
977	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
978	        spells: Which stretch of days each fixed value holds over, per claim.
979	        shape_rows: How big each arrow's push is on each day.
980	        points: The days to work out.
981	
982	    Returns:
983	        One word per day, per claim.
984	    """
985	    named: dict[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]] = {}
986	    untouched: SeriesState = "sampled"
987	    for claim_id in claims:
988	        suppositions = [one for one in spells[claim_id] if one.kind == "do"]
989	        if not suppositions:
990	            named[claim_id] = (untouched,) * len(points)
991	            continue
992	        days: list[SeriesState] = [untouched] * len(points)
993	        for spell in suppositions:
994	            pushing = (
995	                shape_rows[spell.undermined_by.id] > 0.0
996	                if spell.undermined_by is not None
997	                else numpy.zeros(len(points), dtype=bool)
998	            )
999	            for index, day in enumerate(int(one) for one in points):
1000	                if day < spell.starts or (spell.ends is not None and day >= spell.ends):
1001	                    continue
1002	                if spell.undermined_on is None or day < spell.undermined_on:
1003	                    days[index] = "supposed"
1004	                else:
1005	                    days[index] = "pushed" if pushing[index] else "withdrawn"
1006	        named[claim_id] = tuple(days)

1010	def _observation_reach(
1011	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition],
1012	    arrows: Sequence[Link],
1013	    spells: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[_Spell]],
1014	) -> Mapping[PropositionId, frozenset[PropositionId]]:
1015	    """List, for **each** observed claim, the claims that one observation is evidence about.
1016	
1017	    Observing something is done by throwing away the worlds it did not happen in,
1018	    and that changes what the survivors say about the claim's **causes** as much as
1019	    about what it causes — which is why observing reaches upstream and supposing
1020	    does not. One observation reaches the observed claim, everything it leads to,
1021	    everything that leads to it, and everything those causes lead to.
1022	
1023	    **And nothing else, on purpose.** A claim joined to the observed one by no
1024	    chain of arrows in either direction, and sharing no cause with it, is
1025	    independent of what was observed: the right answer for such a claim is the
1026	    answer it already had. Reading it off the surviving worlds only would let a
1027	    coin flip somewhere else move a number nobody touched — the locality rule
1028	    failing by sampling noise rather than by intent — so those claims are read off
1029	    every world instead.
1030	
1031	    **One reach per observation, never the pool of them all.** Two observations in
1032	    pieces of the map that share no arrow and no cause are independent under the
1033	    very model the engine draws from — nothing in the map ties a draw for one piece
1034	    to a draw for the other — so conditioning on one of them says nothing whatever
1035	    about the other's piece. Pooling the reaches would say otherwise: a claim that
1036	    *some* observation is evidence about would be read through *every*
1037	    observation's surviving worlds, and an observation at one end of a map would
1038	    move a claim at the other end that nothing connects it to, by a wash of
1039	    sampling noise. Measured before this was separated: on a map in two pieces,
1040	    observing a claim in one piece moved a claim in the other by **`.083`**.
1041	
1042	    Args:
1043	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
1044	        arrows: The ordinary arrows.
1045	        spells: Which stretch of days each fixed value holds over, per claim.
1046	
1047	    Returns:
1048	        For each observed claim, the claims that observation is evidence about.
1049	        Empty when nothing was observed.
1050	    """
1051	    observed = [
1052	        claim_id
1053	        for claim_id, stretches in spells.items()
1054	        if any(one.kind == "observe" and _still_holds(one) for one in stretches)
1055	    ]
1056	    if not observed:
1057	        return MappingProxyType({})
1058	    walkable: networkx.DiGraph[PropositionId] = networkx.DiGraph()
1059	    walkable.add_nodes_from(sorted(claims))
1060	    walkable.add_edges_from((one.source, one.target) for one in arrows)
1061	    each: dict[PropositionId, frozenset[PropositionId]] = {}
1062	    for claim_id in sorted(observed):
1063	        causes = networkx.ancestors(walkable, claim_id)
1064	        reached = {claim_id} | networkx.descendants(walkable, claim_id) | causes
1065	        for cause in causes:
1066	            reached |= networkx.descendants(walkable, cause)
1067	        each[claim_id] = frozenset(reached)

1075	    return tuple(observed for observed in sorted(reach) if claim_id in reach[observed])

1104	            "evenly spaced points rather than one for every day. Every day is still worked "

1124	def _claim_key(identifier: PropositionId) -> int:
1125	    """Turn a claim's identifier into a number, the same one on every machine.
1126	
1127	    Python's own hashing is stirred differently in every process, which would make
1128	    a world depend on when it was computed. This does not: the same identifier
1129	    always gives the same number, today and next week, here and in a container.

1141	def _standard_normal_quantile(share: Numbers) -> Numbers:
1142	    """Turn "how far along a bell curve" into "how many standard deviations out".
1143	
1144	    A published rational approximation (Peter Acklam's), accurate to about one part
1145	    in a billion, which is millions of times finer than the two significant figures
1146	    anything on screen ever shows. It is written out because the only library that
1147	    ships this function is one this project deliberately does not depend on.
1148	
1149	    Args:
1150	        share: How far along the curve, strictly between 0 and 1.
1151	
1152	    Returns:
1153	        How many standard deviations out that is: 0 in the middle, about 1.28 at
1154	        nine-tenths of the way along.
1155	    """
1156	    a = (
1157	        -3.969683028665376e01,
1158	        2.209460984245205e02,
1159	        -2.759285104469687e02,
1160	        1.383577518672690e02,
1161	        -3.066479806614716e01,
1162	        2.506628277459239e00,
1163	    )
1164	    b = (
1165	        -5.447609879822406e01,
1166	        1.615858368580409e02,
1167	        -1.556989798598866e02,
1168	        6.680131188771972e01,
1169	        -1.328068155288572e01,
1170	    )
1171	    c = (
1172	        -7.784894002430293e-03,
1173	        -3.223964580411365e-01,
1174	        -2.400758277161838e00,
1175	        -2.549732539343734e00,
1176	        4.374664141464968e00,
1177	        2.938163982698783e00,
1178	    )
1179	    d = (7.784695709041462e-03, 3.224671290700398e-01, 2.445134137142996e00, 3.754408661907416e00)
1180	    edge = 0.02425
1181	
1182	    u = numpy.clip(share, TINY, 1.0 - TINY)
1183	    out = numpy.empty_like(u)
1184	
1185	    low, high = u < edge, u > 1.0 - edge
1186	    middle = ~(low | high)
1187	
1188	    q = u[middle] - 0.5
1189	    r = q * q
1190	    out[middle] = (
1191	        (((((a[0] * r + a[1]) * r + a[2]) * r + a[3]) * r + a[4]) * r + a[5])
1192	        * q
1193	        / (((((b[0] * r + b[1]) * r + b[2]) * r + b[3]) * r + b[4]) * r + 1.0)
1194	    )
1195	    for side, tail in ((low, u[low]), (high, 1.0 - u[high])):
1196	        q = numpy.sqrt(-2.0 * numpy.log(tail))
1197	        value = (((((c[0] * q + c[1]) * q + c[2]) * q + c[3]) * q + c[4]) * q + c[5]) / (
1198	            (((d[0] * q + d[1]) * q + d[2]) * q + d[3]) * q + 1.0
1199	        )
1200	        out[side] = value if side is low else -value

1217	    """Turn log-odds back into a likelihood, at the precision one draw is kept to.

1226	def _fitted_halves(belief: Belief) -> tuple[float, float]:
1227	    """Fit the two halves of a stated likelihood and its range, on the log-odds scale.
1228	
1229	    A stated `{p, lo, hi}` is read as a bell curve on the log-odds scale with its
1230	    two halves fitted separately: the middle at `p`, a tenth of the curve below
1231	    `lo` and a tenth above `hi`. The halves are fitted apart because real elicited
1232	    ranges are lopsided, and fitting on log-odds rather than on probability honours
1233	    all three stated numbers exactly and can never leave 0 to 1.
1234	
1235	    Args:
1236	        belief: The stated likelihood with its range.
1237	
1238	    Returns:
1239	        How wide the curve is below the middle, and how wide above.
1240	    """
1241	    middle = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(belief.p)))
1242	    bottom = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(belief.lo)))
1243	    top = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(belief.hi)))
1244	    return (
1245	        max(0.0, (middle - bottom) / NINETIETH_PERCENTILE),
1246	        max(0.0, (top - middle) / NINETIETH_PERCENTILE),
1247	    )

1250	def _version_priors(claim: Proposition, seed: int, versions: int) -> Numbers:
1251	    """Draw one likelihood per version for one claim's prior.
1252	
1253	    The draws are spread evenly over the curve rather than left to clump — a Latin
1254	    hypercube, which here is one stratified column per claim. Each claim's column
1255	    comes from the seed and the claim's own identifier and from nothing else, which
1256	    is what makes a base world and a branch world share their versions: adding a
1257	    claim to the map cannot shift the numbers drawn for any other.
1258	
1259	    Args:
1260	        claim: The claim whose prior is being drawn.
1261	        seed: The one number every draw comes from.
1262	        versions: How many versions to draw.
1263	
1264	    Returns:
1265	        One likelihood per version.
1266	    """
1267	    drawer = numpy.random.default_rng([seed, PARAMS_STREAM, _claim_key(claim.id)])
1268	    strata = (drawer.permutation(versions) + drawer.random(versions)) / versions
1269	    steps = _standard_normal_quantile(strata)
1270	    below, above = _fitted_halves(claim.prior)
1271	    middle = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(claim.prior.p)))
1272	    return _likelihood_of(middle + steps * numpy.where(steps < 0.0, below, above))

1275	def _draw(setup: _Setup, *, seed: int, versions: int, worlds: int) -> _Sample:
1276	    """Run the two loops: every version of the map, and every world under each.
1277	
1278	    Each claim is worked out causes-first, for every draw and every day at once.
1279	    A claim whose value an edit fixed is that value while the fixing holds, and is
1280	    sampled from its own likelihood otherwise. What is kept from each world is the
1281	    **likelihood** the claim came out true with, not the coin flip that came out of
1282	    it — free accuracy, because the number was already worked out.
1283	
1284	    When something was observed, the worlds it did not happen in are thrown away
1285	    and each version then counts by the share of its worlds that survived. That
1286	    takes two passes over the map: which worlds survive is only known once every
1287	    observed claim has been reached, and a claim worked out before then would
1288	    otherwise be averaged over worlds that are about to be discarded.
1289	
1290	    Args:
1291	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
1292	        seed: The one number every draw comes from.
1293	        versions: The outer loop.
1294	        worlds: The inner loop.
1295	
1296	    Returns:
1297	        What each version drew for each prior, what each version answered for each
1298	        claim on each day, how much the worlds inside a version disagreed, how much
1299	        each version counts, and what share of worlds survived.
1300	    """
1301	    priors = {
1302	        claim_id: _version_priors(setup.claims[claim_id], seed, versions)
1303	        for claim_id in setup.order
1304	    }
1305	    coins = {
1306	        claim_id: numpy.random.default_rng([seed, WORLDS_STREAM, _claim_key(claim_id)])
1307	        .random((versions, worlds))
1308	        .astype(DRAWING)
1309	        for claim_id in setup.order
1310	    }
1311	
1312	    alive: Mapping[PropositionId, Flags] = {}
1313	    if setup.observation_reach:
1314	        _, _, alive = _one_pass(setup, priors, coins, versions, worlds, alive, reduce=False)
1315	    likelihood, inner, _ = _one_pass(setup, priors, coins, versions, worlds, alive, reduce=True)
1316	
1317	    # How much each version counts, **per claim**: the share of its worlds that
1318	    # survived the observations that are evidence about that claim, and no others.
1319	    # One pooled share would let an observation weigh a claim it says nothing about.
1320	    counting: dict[PropositionId, Numbers] = {}
1321	    survived_all = numpy.ones((versions, worlds), dtype=bool)
1322	    for observed in sorted(alive):
1323	        survived_all = survived_all & alive[observed]
1324	    for claim_id in setup.order:
1325	        about = _evidence_about(setup.observation_reach, claim_id)
1326	        kept = _surviving_both(alive, about, versions, worlds).sum(axis=1)
1327	        counting[claim_id] = kept.astype(numpy.float64) / worlds
1328	    return _Sample(
1329	        priors=priors,
1330	        likelihood=likelihood,
1331	        inner_spread=inner,
1332	        weights=MappingProxyType(counting),
1333	        survival=float(survived_all.sum()) / float(versions * worlds),
1334	    )

1339	    priors: Mapping[PropositionId, Numbers],
1340	    coins: Mapping[PropositionId, Draws],

1342	    worlds: int,

1344	    *,
1345	    reduce: bool,
1346	) -> tuple[dict[PropositionId, Numbers], dict[PropositionId, Numbers], dict[PropositionId, Flags]]:
1347	    """Walk every claim once, causes first, working out its likelihood in every draw.
1348	
1349	    Args:
1350	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
1351	        priors: What each version drew for each claim's prior.
1352	        coins: One number per claim per world, held the same on every day. It is
1353	            also the same in a base world and a branch world, so the two can be

1361

1364	        version disagreed, and which worlds survived.

1366	    points = len(setup.points)
1367	    shape = (versions, worlds, points)
1368	    truth: dict[PropositionId, Flags] = {}
1369	    fired: dict[PropositionId, Flags] = {}
1370	    answered: dict[PropositionId, Numbers] = {}
1371	    spread: dict[PropositionId, Numbers] = {}
1372	    surviving: dict[PropositionId, Flags] = dict(alive)
1373	
1374	    for claim_id in setup.order:
1375	        baseline = _log_odds(priors[claim_id]).astype(DRAWING)
